condition: daily episodes of excessive food intake followed immediately by self-induced vomiting over 5 months in a young adult woman
level_rationale: Five months of daily episodes of consuming unusually large quantities of food followed immediately by self-induced vomiting of the meal in a 22-year-old woman indicates severe bulimia nervosa requiring psychiatrist evaluation for eating-disorder pharmacotherapy and specialized structured therapy, whereas vomiting a bowlful of fresh red blood right after eating represents acute large-volume upper gastrointestinal hematemesis from a Mallory-Weiss or mucosal tear requiring immediate emergency department resuscitation and endoscopy.

Induces vomiting of the meal immediately afterward

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain young-adult female everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + unsourced college-stress causal belief clause (-att) + single-fact upper-GI hematemesis escalation control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic non-self-harm reference facts (22-year-old woman, daily episodes of eating huge amounts of food over 5 months, and post-meal self-induced vomiting) obeying Hard Limit 7 without naming bulimia, with a 1-word span difference (21 vs 22 words), zero stated negatives, and identical digit multisets across all 6 variants. Under reviewer_notes Rules A and D, escalating only f3 inside the same post-binge emesis context to throwing up a bowlful of fresh red blood right after eating without compounding fainting or extra symptoms shifts care cleanly from psychiatrist evaluation (level 3) to emergency department hemorrhage management (level 4).
